cells_used.xor2: sg13g2_xor2_1, 10 devices. CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF: the brief describes XOR as 'the cell the pass-gate work made cheap (depth 1, 8 devices, XOR and XNOR the same cell with a tap swap)'. That is the qal/pgcell transmission-gate cell, and qal/pgcell's own committed verdict is that restoration gives the saving back -- device-NEUTRAL, 2.38x depth, and the chain still does not compute. The cell whose 3.84 um LEF width sets the AES bit pitch is the PDK's STATIC xor2_1, and it has a 2-HIGH stack on BOTH sides (MP3 over MP2||MP4; MN3+MN4) plus a 2-high pMOS stack on its internal NOR node. It is not a shallow cell. This run uses the PDK cell and reports the pass-gate claim as NOT ADOPTED.

C_THE_MECHANISM_THIS_PHASE_ADDS.statement: An unbuffered QAL bank RETURNS its rail charge at the end of its hold window. A cell output is held up only by its own pull-up from its own bank rail, so when that rail comes down the value is GONE. A signal produced at level j and consumed at level k > j+1 therefore cannot be routed there: it must be RE-DRIVEN at every intervening level by a FORWARDING cell. In CMOS the same signal is a WIRE and costs nothing but capacitance, because a static gate holds its output against a supply that never goes away.
C_THE_MECHANISM_THIS_PHASE_ADDS.why_it_matters_to_the_insight: The insight this campaign run exists to test is 'wiring does the rotate -- a rotate costs ZERO gates and ZERO levels'. That is true within one level boundary. It is FALSE for any value that must survive more than one level, and a cipher round is full of those: ChaCha's a, b, c and d are all live across the whole quarter-round. So the term the insight calls free is, in unbuffered QAL, one inverter per bit per level crossed.
C_THE_MECHANISM_THIS_PHASE_ADDS.how_it_is_enforced_not_assumed: cg.Chain.evaluate() REFUSES to build a netlist in which any cell reads a level older than k-1. A vehicle that needs forwarding cannot be constructed without paying for it, so the forwarding census is a property of the netlist rather than an estimate.
C_THE_MECHANISM_THIS_PHASE_ADDS.kogge_stone_is_the_favourable_case: Kogge-Stone is UNIFORM-DEPTH: every prefix cell reads only the level directly above it. That is exactly the property unbuffered QAL needs, and it is a real structural argument for the parallel-prefix form. A ripple CPA is not uniform-depth: bit i's propagate must survive i carry levels, so its forwarding cost grows as O(W^2).
C_THE_MECHANISM_THIS_PHASE_ADDS.sha_slice_corroboration: This run's INDEPENDENTLY reconstructed 8-bit ripple CPA is 164 cells over 10 levels. The committed qal/sha256 block that measured so badly was 161 cells over 14 banks with an 8-BIT RIPPLE CPA. Two independent constructions landing on the same size is evidence the reconstruction is faithful, and it is pre-registered here as a check to be scored, not as a claim.

aes_shiftrows.permutation: column-major 4x4 state, byte index 4c+r holds s[r][c], row r rotated LEFT by r bytes. Verified against the FIPS-197 index permutation [0,5,10,15,4,9,14,3,8,13,2,7,12,1,6,11].
aes_shiftrows.floorplan_STATED: the 16 bytes sit in the natural AES 4x4 tile grid, one tile per byte, with the 8 bit-slices of a byte side by side across a tile. A column pitch is therefore 8 bit pitches, and the wrap is routed the short way round.
aes_shiftrows.which_pitch_is_right: the cell that must physically fit per bit is the one being placed. AddRoundKey places xor2_1, whose LEF SIZE is 3.84 um, so 3.84 um is the HONEST pitch for this vehicle and 4.608 fF/bit is its nominal load. The 1.00 um column is the brief's own geometry and is carried as the optimistic end.

chacha_rotates.formula_DERIVED: bit i -> bit (i+r) mod W: (W-r) bits travel r pitches and r bits travel (W-r) -- mean 2r(W-r)/W bit pitches (Phase 1's formula, reused).

D_THE_WIRE_GEOMETRY_DERIVED.relation_to_phase1: Phase 1 measured the signal-wire QAL/CMOS ratio declining through 1.003x at Cw = 2.400 fF, 0.964x at 3.489 fF and 0.749x -- a LOSS -- at 9.216 fF, and 9.216 fF was the ONE row that also stopped computing (fcrit S3 27/32). AES's nominal 4.608 fF/bit and ChaCha's nominal 7.767 fF/bit both sit INSIDE that decline. Phase 2 therefore expects to be measuring the losing part of Phase 1's curve, and says so before running.

F_ROWS_PRE_STATED.NOT_SIMULATED_and_why: the 32-bit RIPPLE CPA is 34 levels and 2576 cells and needs 68 ZCS probe decks. It is reported STRUCTURALLY (exactly, from the netlist) and is NOT simulated. Its level count and cell count are netlist facts, not estimates; its energy is NOT claimed. The full 4x quarter-round is likewise reported as a level-structure composition over MEASURED level times and MEASURED per-level energies, and every composed number is labelled COMPOSED.
F_ROWS_PRE_STATED.beat_selection_rule: T is not guessed. For each vehicle, T starts at an estimate scaled from the qal/widebank sibling's own N-sweep (DERIVED: t_hop scales as sqrt(C_tank), and C_bank(xor2) / C_bank(inv) = 3.22 at N = 128, so t_hop x1.80 and T from widebank's accepted 580 ps to ~1045 ps) and ESCALATES by 1.35x until the row passes G2/G6/G7/G11 or four escalations are spent. Every attempt is recorded with its wall time, pass/fail and the gate that failed -- the same protocol qal/widebank used.
F_ROWS_PRE_STATED.runtime_management: AES is 1792 devices over 3 levels with a ~8 ns span; K32 is 2320 devices over 7 levels. Concurrency is held at <= 6 heavy Xyce processes, per the brief. Probe decks are single-hop windows and are cheap. If a single row exceeds 3600 s it is abandoned, reported as abandoned, and the vehicle falls back to the next smaller width with the scoping stated -- it is NOT silently replaced by a narrower slice, which is the error the campaign made once (a narrow carry-chain slice generalised to a cipher).

G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS._status: written before any Xyce run of Phase 2. I commit to reporting these whichever way they land and to naming every one I miss. Phase 1 scored 2 right, 3 partly, 3 wrong and said so; the same standard applies here.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q0_the_adder_form_INVERTS_between_techno: In QAL the parallel-prefix form wins structurally and will win measurably: 32-bit ripple is 4.857x the levels and 5.111x the cells of 32-bit Kogge-Stone, because the ripple's O(W^2) forwarding tax is a QAL-only cost. In CMOS the SAME comparison goes the OTHER WAY: CMOS needs no forwarding at all, so a CMOS 32-bit ripple is roughly W x (a full adder, ~24 devices) = ~770 devices against a CMOS Kogge-Stone's ~2300. PREDICTION: the measured QAL energy ratio ripple/KS at 8 bits is >= 1.8x in the ripple's disfavour, while the CMOS device count goes the other way by >= 2x. If that holds, 'the adder form was a harness choice, not a property of the algorithm' is TRUE of the algorithm and FALSE of the technology: the choice is forced differently in QAL than in CMOS.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q1_the_beat: N = 128 xor2_1 will need T >= 900 ps, against the widebank sibling's 580 ps for N = 128 INVERTERS, i.e. the CELL dominates the population. Predicted band 900-1600 ps, accepted on the escalation rule.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q2_per_gate_energy: the widebank sibling measured 3.807 fJ per gate for N = 128 inverters. XOR2 is 5x the devices. PREDICTION: 8-20 fJ per gate WITH wire, i.e. well above the ideal-PWL floor of 3.5227 fJ, so the N_min ~ 52 energy argument the brief invokes does NOT rescue this vehicle -- N = 128 is far above N_min and the vehicle still loses.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q3_AES_energy_vs_CMOS: PREDICTION: QAL LOSES on energy at AES's own nominal wire load. Phase 1 measured the signal-wire ratio at 1.003x (Cw 2.400), 0.964x (3.489) and 0.749x (9.216); AES's nominal 4.608 fF/bit sits inside that decline, so I predict 0.80-0.98x, most likely 0.85-0.95x. If it comes out above 1.0x I have mispredicted and will say so.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q4_AES_speed_vs_CMOS: a CMOS AddRoundKey is ONE gate delay. A QAL AddRoundKey is a full rail hop plus a settle. PREDICTION: QAL is 7-15x SLOWER on this level, and there is NO configuration in Phase 2 where QAL is faster.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q5_gates: at the nominal wire on matched tanks I predict G7 PASSES (the tank is matched, which is why matched tanks are mandatory) and the committed 90 % settling bar FAILS, with fcrit S3 still passing; at the HIGH wire figure (6.700 fF/bit) I predict fcrit S3 FAILS, by analogy with Phase 1's 9.216 fF row which failed at +3.263 mV against a 19.323 mV budget.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q6_sha_slice_corroboration: my independently reconstructed 8-bit ripple (164 cells, 10 levels) should land within 2x of the committed qal/sha256 block's per-gate energy (161 cells, 14 banks, 8-bit ripple CPA). If it does not, one of the two constructions is wrong and I will identify which rather than reporting the discrepancy as a result.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q7_the_quarter_round: a 32-bit ChaCha quarter-round with a Kogge-Stone adder is 32 levels, therefore 32 rail hops. PREDICTION: per-op time 20-40 ns against a CMOS critical path of 1-3 ns, so QAL loses on speed at the op level by 10-30x. With a ripple adder it is 140 levels and loses by ~5x more again.
G_MY_PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS.Q8_the_verdict_I_expect: NEITHER vehicle puts QAL ahead of CMOS on energy OR on speed. The only term in this campaign where QAL beats CMOS on a real capacitance remains Phase 1's RAIL/clock-distribution wire (2.0-5.9x), which is not the cipher datapath term. I expect the deliverable of Phase 2 to be the MECHANISM -- that QAL converts wires into cells, and that this falls hardest on exactly the rotate-and-carry structures the insight nominated as its best case. If a vehicle wins I will say so as plainly as I am saying I expect it not to.

H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.ideal_CMOS_supply: the CMOS twin's VDD is an ideal voltage source. Direction: FAVOURS CMOS, so every reported ratio is conservative for QAL.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.ideal_tank_precharge: the QAL tank is a linear capacitor pre-charged by .ic; its generation is not costed. Direction: FAVOURS QAL. Every QAL row is a BOUND on that account.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.ideal_gate_drives: VHI and every transfer/park gate PWL are ideal sources; their energy IS metered (egt, ehi) but their generation is not. Direction: FAVOURS QAL.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.held_sources: primary inputs, the AES round key and the adders' A and B words are ideal DC sources, legal at any level because a held register's supply does not return. Metered by qi1/ei1. Applied IDENTICALLY to both technologies, so it cancels in the ratio; it does bound the absolute numbers.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.first_cycle_energy: Phase 1 AMENDMENT A4 applies unchanged: the committed deck is SINGLE-SHOT and its rails do not return to 0, so every energy here is a FIRST-CYCLE energy. A steady-state QAL cycle would start each rail part-charged, so either the swing collapses or the rail must be drained at a cost this deck family does not measure. It cancels in the difference and is identical on both sides; it bounds the interpretation.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.lumped_wire_C: Cw is a lumped linear capacitor, applied IDENTICALLY to both sides. Phase 1 MEASURED this idealisation against a 3-segment pi RC ladder carrying the PDK's own 8.24 ohm and found 0.004 fJ of 220 fJ -- 0.01 %. Validated, not declared.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.no_via_or_jog_capacitance: the permutation wire is straight min-width Metal2 of the mean length. Vias and jogs are excluded. Direction: UNDERSTATES the wire, hence understates whichever side wire favours.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.sizing_rule: C_bank(k) is DERIVED by scaling the committed MEASURED 4.497375 fF per inverter cell by the cell's device count. It is a SIZING rule, not a measurement; the measured secant C of every level is reported beside it and the rule's error is reported, exactly as qal/widebank reports its own 1.63x.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.leakage: sg13lv_compat.sp discards ad/as/pd/ps, so the default PD = 1.00 um clips the STI-edge term on the 1.12 um pMOS and every implied leakage figure is a LOWER bound.
H_BOOKINGS_EVERY_ONE_A_BOUND.forwarding_cell_choice: forwarding uses ONE inverter per bit per level, which flips polarity -- and in the alternating-polarity parallel prefix the flip is exactly what the next stage wants, so no polarity repair is spent. This is the CHEAPEST physical forwarding available, so the reported forwarding tax is a LOWER bound on QAL's cost.

J_LABELS.MEASURED: read off a .mt0 or .prn produced by this run, or read directly out of a committed PDK file
J_LABELS.DERIVED: computed in closed form from MEASURED quantities or from the netlist's own structure, with the formula stated
J_LABELS.ASSUMED: neither -- stated as such, with what it would take to remove it
J_LABELS.COMPOSED: summed or scaled across separately MEASURED levels. Level times are measured end to end and never composed; an OP time that sums measured level times is labelled COMPOSED wherever it appears.
J_LABELS.BOOKING: modelled as an ideal source or element; its row is a BOUND and the direction of the bias is named
